topic: describing direction, form, and strength in scatter plots
subtitle: Reading a scatter plot, then naming its direction, its form, and how strong it is

problems.desc: Written description of direction. Full credit for saying the association is positive, or increasing: as the hours of revision go up, the test scores go up too. Accept any wording that names the direction and says which way both variables move; naming the direction with no reference to the two variables earns partial credit only.

Written description of direction. Full credit for saying the association is negative, or decreasing: the more hours of television watched, the lower the test score. Accept any wording that names the direction and links it to both variables; a bare word with no reference to the plot earns partial credit only.

Written description of form. Full credit for saying the form is not linear: the points rise to a peak in the early afternoon and then fall, so a curve fits them and a single straight line does not. Accept any wording that rejects a straight line and describes the rise-then-fall shape.

Written description of strength. Full credit for saying the association is very strong, because every point lies on the same straight line with no scatter around it, so knowing the hours worked tells you the pay exactly. Accept any wording that ties strength to how closely the points hug a line.

problems.slot: the range of the plotted values

problems.desc: Written description of direction. Full credit for saying there is no association, or no clear direction: the points are scattered with no upward or downward trend, so shoe size tells you nothing about the number of books read. Accept any wording that says the direction is neither positive nor negative.

problems.slot: the value at the unusual point

problems.desc: Circled outlier with a reason. Full credit for circling the point at 7 hours with a value of 30 and saying why it is unusual: the other six points climb by about 2 each time and this one jumps far above that pattern. Accept any wording that names the point and compares it with the trend of the rest; circling with no reason earns partial credit only.

problems.slot: the median of the plotted values

problems.desc: Written description of direction and strength together. Full credit for saying the association is positive but only moderately strong: the points climb from left to right, yet they zig-zag around the trend instead of sitting on one line. Accept any wording that names the direction AND comments on the amount of scatter; naming only one of the two earns partial credit.

problems.slot: the difference between the last and first values

problems.desc: Written description of form. Full credit for saying the form is not linear: the first few points rise gently and the later ones rise much faster, so the pattern bends upward instead of following one straight line. Accept any wording that contrasts the flat start with the steep finish.

Written description of all three features. Full credit for a sentence that names the direction (negative: older cars cost less), the form (linear, since the points fall in a nearly straight line) and the strength (strong, because the points sit very close to that line). Accept any wording covering all three; a response naming only one or two features earns partial credit.

problems.slot: the value at the outlying point

problems.desc: Written description with the outlier removed. Full credit for saying that the point at week 6, where only 5 pages were read, sits far below the rest, and that once it is set aside the remaining points show a strong positive linear association. Accept any wording that separates the unusual point from the pattern of the others and describes that pattern.
